chunks: Abu Basir narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
“In bidding farewell to the month of Ramadan, say: O Allah, You have said in Your Book sent down upon Your sent Prophet, and Your word is the truth:
“The month of Ramadan is that in which the Qur'an was sent down as guidance for mankind, and clear proofs of guidance and the criterion.”

And this month of Ramadan has passed, so I ask You by Your noble Face and Your perfect words: if there remains upon me a sin that You have not forgiven for me, and You intend to call me to account for it, or punish me for it, or reckon me by it, then let not the dawn of this night rise, nor this month pass completely, except that You have forgiven it for me, O Most Merciful of the merciful.

O Allah, to You belongs all praise, with all Your praises, for all Your blessings, the first of them and the last of them: that which You have said for Yourself among them, and that which the praising creatures have said—those diligent in Your remembrance and in gratitude to You, whom You have helped to perform Your due right from the classes of Your creation, from the near angels, the Prophets, the messengers, and the various speaking beings and those who glorify You from all the worlds—for that You caused us to reach the month of Ramadan, while upon us are of Your blessings, and with us are of Your apportioned gifts, Your beneficence, and the manifest abundance of Your favor, what we cannot enumerate.

So to You belongs everlasting, enduring, increasing, perpetual, eternal praise that does not come to an end through endless time. Exalted is Your praise. You helped us in it until You enabled us to complete its fasting and its standing in salat (prayer), so whatever there was from us in it of righteousness, gratitude, or remembrance—

O Allah, then accept it from us with the best of Your acceptance, Your overlooking, Your pardon, Your forbearance, Your forgiveness, and the reality of Your good pleasure, until You cause us in it to attain every sought good and abundant granted gift, and secure us in it from every feared thing, or brought affliction, or acquired sin.

O Allah, I ask You by the greatest matter with which any of Your creation has asked You, by Your noble names, the beauty of Your praise, and Your special supplication, to send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and to make this month of ours the greatest month of Ramadan that has passed over us since You brought us down to the world.

As blessing in the safeguarding of my religion, the deliverance of my soul, the fulfillment of my need, the granting of intercession in my requests, the completion of blessing upon me, the turning away of evil from me, and the clothing of well-being for me; and that by Your mercy You make me among those for whom You have reserved Laylat al-Qadr and made it for him better—
in the greatest reward, the most noble stored treasure, the finest gratitude, the longest life, and the most lasting ease.

O Allah, and I ask You by Your mercy, Your might, Your abundance, Your pardon, Your blessings, Your majesty, and the ancientness of Your beneficence and favor, that You do not make it the last covenant from us with the month of Ramadan, until You cause us to reach it again in the coming year in the best state, and let us know its crescent among those looking at it and recognizing it, within Your fullest well-being, Your most complete blessing, Your widest mercy, and Your greatest apportioned share.

O Allah, O my Lord, besides whom I have no lord, do not make this farewell of mine to it a farewell of ending, nor the last covenant of meeting from me, until You show it to me again in the coming year amid the most abundant blessings and the best hope, while I am for You upon the best faithfulness.
“Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication.”

O Allah, hear my supplication, have mercy on my pleading, my humility before You, my lowliness, and my reliance upon You. For I am surrendered to You, and I do not hope for success or well-being except through You and from You. So bestow Your favor upon me—exalted is Your praise and sanctified are Your names—and let me reach the month of Ramadan while I am protected from every disliked thing and danger, and keep me away from all calamities. Praise belongs to Allah, who helped us in fasting this month until He caused us to reach its last night.”

key_terms.الدُّعَاءِ: supplication, which Allah is described as hearing
key_terms.الْعَافِيَةِ: well-being, protection, and soundness sought from Allah
key_terms.الْقُرْآنُ: the Qur'an, described here as guidance and criterion revealed in Ramadan
key_terms.ذَنْبٌ: a sin for which the supplicant seeks forgiveness before the month ends
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the sacred month of fasting in which the Qur'an was revealed
key_terms.صِيَامِهِ: its fasting, referring to the fasting of Ramadan
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ الْقَدْرِ: Laylat al-Qadr, the special night reserved with immense reward
key_terms.وَدَاعِ: farewelling or bidding farewell in the context of the end of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What supplication is recited when bidding farewell to the month of Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a supplication for bidding farewell to the month of Ramadan, centered on seeking forgiveness, acceptance of worship, and gratitude for being enabled to fast and pray. It invokes Qur'anic verses about Ramadan and Laylat al-Qadr, asking Allah to let the supplicant reach future Ramadans in wellbeing, faithfulness, and divine mercy.
